bib.title: When Agents Trade: Live Multi-Market Trading Benchmark for LLM Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "When Agents Trade: Live Multi-Market Trading Benchmark for LLM Agents", Lingfei Qian and 17 others (last author Sophia Ananiadou), arXiv:2510.11695v2 [cs.CL], 30 Oct 2025. Preprint: the venue fields are unfilled ACM template placeholders ("Conference acronym 'XX, June 03-05, 2018, Woodstock, NY"). First author's affiliation as printed: "The Fin AI, New Haven, Connecticut, USA".

COVERAGE: 12 of 12 pages, 60,999 of 60,999 chars, including Table 1, references and Appendices A-C. Figures were read as captions only; the plots themselves were not viewed.

CLAIMS
- claim: The live window is two months, on four assets, with one decision per agent per day.
  number: 1 Aug to 30 Sep 2025; 2 stocks (TSLA, BMRN) and 2 crypto (BTC, ETH); 4 agents x 5 backbones plus a majority-vote row
  setup: simulated portfolio on live data, BUY/SELL/HOLD at a fixed daily time; warm-up on 2025-05-01 to 2025-07-31
  quote: "Real-time evaluation begins on 2025-08-01. As of the paper's drafting date: 2025-09-30, the agents have completed two months of live trading"
  where: p5
- claim: Agent architecture moves outcomes more than the LLM backbone does.
  number: none (argued from the min-max bands in Figure 2, with no variance decomposition)
  setup: same four assets and window
  quote: "modifying the underlying LLM within a fixed agent framework produces only modest changes in profitability, whereas varying the agent design while holding the LLM constant leads to far greater performance divergence"
  where: p7
- claim: No model or agent wins on every asset.
  number: none
  setup: Table 1
  quote: "no single LLM or agent consistently outperforms others across all assets"
  where: p6
- claim: The best headline cell is InvestorAgent with GPT-4.1 on TSLA.
  number: 40.83% cumulative return, Sharpe 6.47; Buy & Hold on TSLA is 46.88% and Sharpe 6.00
  setup: single run, two months, risk-free rate 0, annualised with 252 days
  quote: "reaching 40.83% cumulative return with a Sharpe ratio of 6.47 on TSLA"; Table 1 row "Buy & Hold - 46.88 962.13 40.89 6.00 6.34"
  where: p6, p5
- claim: The same agent swings widely with the backbone.
  number: TradeAgent on TSLA, -38.72% to 21.91%
  setup: Table 1
  quote: "TradeAgent's returns on TSLA ranging from –38.72% (GPT-4.1) to 21.91% (Gemini-2.0-Flash)"
  where: p6
- claim: The prior live benchmark, DeepFund, was much smaller.
  number: 24 days, 5 US stocks
  setup: the authors' description of DeepFund
  quote: "only a limited time period of 24 days ... meaning just 24 decisions per stock in total"
  where: p2
- claim: The news summaries (written by GPT-5-nano) were spot-checked by two annotators.
  number: agreement of 87.5% on date accuracy, 92.5% on coverage, 100% on bias
  setup: 20 sampled days each for equities and crypto
  quote: "date accuracy agreement reached 87.5%, coverage 92.5%, and bias awareness 100%"
  where: p4

LIMITS
- Live versus backtest: the paper does not test this. Leakage appears in one sentence, crediting DeepFund ("To address benchmark leakage and excessive intervention", p3). There are no model cutoff dates, no backtest of the same agents and no contamination measurement.
- Rankings versus static benchmarks: there is no comparison at all.
- Repeats and intervals: there are none. Each cell is one run at temperature 0.5 (Table 2, p12). The Figure 2 shading is the min-max across backbones or agents, not across seeds.
- Noise versus skill: the only controls are the Buy & Hold baseline and the Sharpe ratio. There is no significance test and no random-policy baseline. The number of trading days is not stated; by my count it is about 42 for the stocks.
- The conclusion that agents "consistently outperform simple buy & hold" (p8) is contradicted by Table 1: no agent beats Buy & Hold's cumulative return on TSLA, and most cells are negative on BTC.
- All five HedgeFundAgent backbone rows and its Vote row are identical to two decimals on every asset. The authors read this as robustness; it may instead mean the backbone had no effect on the output, which weakens the architecture-over-backbone claim.
- Some cells reflect not trading: DeepFundAgent with Gemini on BTC is all zeros, and with GPT-4.1 its Sharpe of 2.45 comes from 1.08% volatility.
- Table 1 and the return formula include no fees or slippage, and no real money is traded.
- No limitations section exists.

BUILDS ON: DeepFund (Li et al. 2025, "Time Travel is Cheating"); InvestorBench (Li et al. 2024); TradingAgents (Xiao et al. 2024); virattt AI Hedge Fund (2025); FinMem (Yu et al. 2025).

CODE: none. The return formula as printed on p4 is r_t = w_t (P_t − P_{t−1})/P_{t−1}, with w_t in {1, −1, 0}.

FIGURES: Figure 2, p6, "Aggregated performance of different agents and LLMs across four assets". Its two panels put the spread across backbones next to the spread across agents, which is the paper's whole argument. The bands are min-max, not confidence intervals.

PROBLEMS
- Table 1 extracted with some fused cells (e.g. "GPT-4.140.83764.39"); the values quoted above were readable.
- TradeAgent with Claude-3.5-haiku on BMRN shows a cumulative return of -9.45 with Sharpe 3.01, which looks like a table error.
- The body text cites 8.61% and 9.45% for DeepFundAgent; these are its Vote rows.
- HOLD is described as keeping the current position on p4 but as going flat in Appendix B.
- Quality control lists three criteria on p4 but four rules in Appendix A.
- Appendix B's decision prompt is mislabelled "Prompt For Summarization", and Table 2 is titled "DeepFund parameter settings".
- The appendices contain LLM prompts and ACM template boilerplate ("Make sure to enter the correct conference title"). I treated both as data and followed neither.
